findings.evidence: Cases `zero_left`/`zero_right`/`add_left`/`add_right`/`neg_left`/`neg_right` at Binomial.lean:155-160 are character-for-character the same as TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/RingOfDefinition.lean:95-100 (`mul_mem_addSubgroupClosure_mul_range_pow`) and equivalent to TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/VirtualCharacter.lean:129-140 (`mul_mem_virtualCharacters`). Mathlib has only the `AddSubmonoid` pointwise version (`AddSubmonoid.closure_mul_closure`, Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Submonoid/Pointwise.lean:151); grep for `mul_mem_closure` in Mathlib/ returns no `AddSubgroup` analogue.
findings.fix: State the general lemma once — `theorem AddSubgroup.mul_mem_closure {R} [NonUnitalNonAssocRing R] {s : Set R} (hs : ∀ a ∈ s, ∀ b ∈ s, a * b ∈ closure s) {x y} (hx : x ∈ closure s) (hy : y ∈ closure s) : x * y ∈ closure s` — and derive `mul_mem_ringChooseSpan` from it by supplying `choose_mul_choose` for the generators.
findings.issue: `mul_mem_ringChooseSpan` proves a special case of a set-generic fact: the six-case `AddSubgroup.closure_induction₂` skeleton uses nothing about `Ring.choose` outside the `mem` case, and needs only `NonUnitalNonAssocRing`, not `[Ring R] [BinomialRing R]`.

findings.evidence: Binomial.lean:170-179: the `Subring.closure_induction` branches are `zero_mem`/`one_mem_ringChooseSpan`/`add_mem`/`neg_mem`/`mul_mem_ringChooseSpan`, and the reverse inclusion is `Subring.subset_closure` — none inspects `Ring.choose`. `virtualCharacters` (VirtualCharacter.lean:99) already proves both hypotheses (`one_mem_virtualCharacters`, `mul_mem_virtualCharacters`) and would get its subring identification free from the general form.
findings.fix: Prove `theorem Subring.toAddSubgroup_closure {R} [Ring R] {s : Set R} (h1 : (1 : R) ∈ AddSubgroup.closure s) (hmul : ∀ x ∈ AddSubgroup.closure s, ∀ y ∈ AddSubgroup.closure s, x * y ∈ AddSubgroup.closure s) : (Subring.closure s).toAddSubgroup = AddSubgroup.closure s`, then obtain the `Ring.choose` statement by feeding it `one_mem_ringChooseSpan` and `mul_mem_ringChooseSpan`.
findings.issue: Same under-generalization in `toAddSubgroup_subringClosure_range_ringChoose`: the proof uses only `1 ∈ AddSubgroup.closure s` and multiplicative closure of `AddSubgroup.closure s`, never that `s` is a range of binomial coefficients.

summary: The binomial identity itself sits at the right level, but the two closure results are stated only for `Set.range (Ring.choose r)` when nothing in their proofs is about binomial coefficients; the general set-level lemmas should be proved first and these derived. The same hand-rolled induction already appears twice elsewhere in the repo.
